facts.value: Reads All-Star progress from gm_80473A18._94[0], upcoming count and character IDs from _94[1] and subsequent bytes, and roster IDs from x76. Character IDs become animation frames for models attached to joints 58–60 and roster joints 29–54. The periodic reward path initializes a fallback position, optionally replaces it from marker 0xDC, and obtains a reward/display ID from Ground_801C5840; an ID other than -1 is passed to the collectible request and trophy-system notification. Despite its local name, line_id is not a collision-line lookup result. Initialization finally registers onJointCollision with Ground user data and clears xC4.

facts.value: Reward creation is attempted when progress is divisible by the configured interval and the reward/display ID is not -1. Successful marker lookup is not required: missing marker 0xDC preserves the initialized fallback position. The code does not locally validate a nonzero divisor or clamp the upcoming count to its four-byte temporary list and three destination joints. Roster entries equal to 33 are skipped. Initialization ends by installing the collision callback and clearing xC4; the collectible request's result is ignored before trophy-system notification.

facts.rationale: Corrects collision-line terminology and distinguishes callback registration from synchronous predicate consumption while preserving cross-file item persistence.
facts.value: HEAL coordinates three state paths. Persistent Heart slots are requested only while their availability entries are nonzero; successful special Heart Containers retain their slot indices and clear those entries on destruction. Periodic reward requests require progress divisible by the configured interval and a reward/display ID other than -1, not collision-line validity; missing marker 0xDC leaves the fallback position {0,40,0}. Object 1's qualifying numeric collision filter sets xC4, and a null-safe predicate reports it without mutation. Each object process registers that predicate with Ground_801C3D44, advances transient records and clears xC4. The shared helper stores the predicate rather than invoking it synchronously, so precise polling-versus-reset order belongs to the wider scheduler.
